# jamfplatform_pro_static_mobile_device_group (Data Source)

Use this only when the group must belong to a Jamf Pro site. For everything else prefer `jamfplatform_device_group` with `device_type = "mobile"` and `group_type = "static"`, which manages the same mobile device group across Jamf Platform and is the supported path; it has no site attribute, which is the one thing this adds. Look one up by identifier or by exact name, and supply exactly one of the two. Membership comes back with it, so this is where to look up which mobile devices a group holds.

**Required Jamf permissions**

Jamf lists this under **Platform environment** scope (preferred for new integrations) or **Tenant** scope. You choose an integration's scope when you create it in Jamf Account, and cannot change it afterwards. The provider names the scopes it accepts when you configure it, and for a few families that is wider than Jamf lists here. Grant the API integration the following permissions in Jamf Account — see [Getting started with the Platform API](https://developer.jamf.com/platform-api/reference/getting-started-with-platform-api). `Category` and `Permission` name the section and row of the permission picker; `Actions` are the boxes to tick within that row.

| Category | Permission | Actions | API capability |
|---|---|---|---|
| Inventory | Device groups | Read | `device-groups` |
| Inventory | Devices | Read | `devices` |

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "jamfplatform_pro_static_mobile_device_group" "example_by_id" {
  id = "17"
}

data "jamfplatform_pro_static_mobile_device_group" "example_by_name" {
  name = "Loaner iPads"
}

# The singular lookup is where membership comes from: the plural data source
# reports how many devices a group holds, not which ones.
output "loaner_members" {
  value = data.jamfplatform_pro_static_mobile_device_group.example_by_name.assigned_mobile_device_ids
}

output "static_mobile_device_group_example_by_id" {
  value = data.jamfplatform_pro_static_mobile_device_group.example_by_id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `id` (String) Jamf Pro identifier for the group. Mutually exclusive with `name`.
- `name` (String) Group display name, matched exactly. Mutually exclusive with `id`.
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `assigned_mobile_device_ids` (List of String) Jamf Pro identifiers of the mobile devices in the group, in the order Jamf Pro reports them.
- `description` (String) Note Jamf Pro keeps with the group.
- `member_count` (Number) Mobile devices Jamf Pro counts in the group.
- `platform_id` (String) Identifier for this group across Jamf Platform, which is how a blueprint or a compliance benchmark targets it.
- `site_id` (String) Jamf Pro site the group belongs to. `-1` means no site.

<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `read` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
